items.articleText: ManyForge: a new manipulation framework - Projects - Open Robotics Discourse ManyForge: a new manipulation framework Projects pastoriomarco November 5, 2026, 12:08pm 1 Hi everyone! I mentioned this project at ROSCon Italy a couple of days ago but it was literally just released! Meet ManyForge , which is an evolution of ManyMove . It’s not just its “newer version”: it’s redesigned from ground up around a few core concepts, some of which I took directly from @scastro ’s RoboPlan (the planner I use as standard in ManyForge): The core is ROS-free: all core ManyForge components are C++ or Python and don’t depend on ROS. Realtime-sensitive functionalities are C++, never Python. ManyForge is the authority for all important functionalities (scene, collisions, execution, stop), while ROS is the integration layer: stock ros2_control/JTC and vendor drivers through adapters. Mock, Sim and Real behave the same, so you can build a program on Mock and run it on Isaac Sim or a real robot. The best part for UX is the GUI (the Composer): you build programs as behavior trees in a dedicated drag&drop editor allowing most of the functionalities you’d expect to ease programming a manipulator: a 3D scene where you place and move objects with gizmos, or edit them in the object editor; manual moves with a ghost robot that shows where the arm will end up (collision-checked) before you send it; Draft + Apply, so nothing changes on the cell until you say so; live robot state, I/O and stop handling right in the same window. Honestly, it’s a huge application and it’s still in Beta, and I’m the first to recognize it would require more documentation and educational material to be understood correctly. I’m working on it. In the meantime, I’m making it as much operable and discoverable by LLMs as possible, so any frontier model should be able to install it and explain how it works in detail without much trouble. A note about the development process: the public repository is for deployment and I’m using AI coding assistants heavily. But all development is based on a (for now private) Specs repo that is the authority on what each and every component of ManyForge is, what it does and how, in painstaking detail. Every change is checked against the Specs, reviewed independently and run through thousands of tests, sanitizer builds and stress runs, plus live checks on Mock, Isaac Sim and the real robot, so even structural changes don’t break execution. Still, since I am the one doing all the architectural and design decisions, I’m pretty sure this could be better and I’m very open to discussing architectural and design choices, hardening, and also to introduce useful functionalities. 2 Likes Related topics Topic Replies Views Activity ManyMove - A simple manipulation framework - What, Why and How Projects 2 517 June 11, 2025 ManyMove – C++/Python Behavior Trees for Robot Manipulators (Looking for Feedback and Tips) Projects 9 1122 March 28, 2025 [Release] LinkForge v1.4.0: A Programmable Robot Description Engine (URDF/SRDF) ROS General release , ros2 , simulation , robotics , physics 2 190 June 2, 2026 ManyMove integration with Isaac SIM 5.0 ROS General 0 241 August 30, 2025 LinkForge v1.3.0 — The Linter & Bridge for Robotics ROS General release , ros2 , simulation , ros2_control , open-source 0 188 March 2, 2026

The same release will also add robotiq_driver , robotiq_msgs and the other robotiq-ros packages to the build farm for the first time. Kilted is not affected and stays on PickNik’s 0.0.1 until its end of life. Because apt upgrades can’t be undone, here is what will change for you. What stays the same: the package names, the file paths, the robotiq_gripper macro and its arguments, the joint and link names, the robotiq_driver/RobotiqGripperHardwareInterface plugin and the RobotiqActivationController . The 0.0.1 names sim_ignition , sim_isaac , fake_sensor_commands , urdf/robotiq_gripper.ros2_control.xacro and the connected_to argument of ur_to_robotiq still work, but print a deprecation warning. We expanded the released descriptions of Kinova’s ros2_kortex, Clearpath’s clearpath_common and Husarion’s husarion_components_description against the new packages on every distro where they are released, and our CI will continue to check them. What changes: The version goes from 0.0.1 to 1.x. Installing robotiq_controllers now also installs robotiq_driver and robotiq_msgs . With mock hardware (use_fake_hardware:=true ), /joint_states carries only the driven joint, robotiq_85_left_knuckle_joint . robot_state_publisher derives the other finger joints from the URDF’s mimic tags. If your code reads the other finger joints from /joint_states , please tell us. In Gazebo, the plugin is gz_ros2_control/GazeboSimSystem instead of ign_ros2_control/IgnitionSystem . gz_ros2_control registers both names. With sim_isaac , the plugin is topic_based_ros2_control/TopicBasedSystem instead of isaac_ros2_control/IsaacSystem , on the same topics. You also get more state interfaces and more controllers. See the README . If something breaks: please open an issue on robotiq-ros . Until it’s fixed, you can build 0.0.1 from source (the 0.0.1 tag of ros2_robotiq_gripper), or point apt at the snapshots.ros.org repository from before the sync. Timeline: On 2026-11-18, if nobody raises a blocker: we open the rosdistro PRs. A few days after each merge: the packages reach ros-testing. We’ll post here, so you can try them before they reach the main repository. At each distro’s next sync: the packages reach the main repository. Questions and concerns are welcome here. 2 Likes jaharoni November 5, 2026, 11:46pm 2 Thanks for the heads-up on the upstream repository consolidation into robotiq-ros ! items.title: Looking for research gaps in cooperative AUVs and underwater communication
items.summary: Hi everyone, I have a Master’s degree in Computer Science, with a background in computer networks and IoT. I’m currently looking for a research topic for a conference paper on Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs). I’ve been reading recent papers about cooperative AUVs, formation control, path planning, and underwater acoustic communication. I noticed that many studies already address packet loss, communication delays, and event-triggered communication. I’m trying to find a specific research problem that has not been fully solved yet. I’m especially interested in a topic that I can investigate using Python simulation, without physical robots. For those working in underwater robotics or related fields: What are some important research gaps or practical challenges that current studies still don’t address well? Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Today, we’re rolling out Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, and making it generally available across the Gemini API and Gemini for business . Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash introduces native 15-second video creation, multi-turn conversational editing capabilities, and enhanced reference following. We have dropped the price 30% from Gemini Omni 1.1 making it available at $0.07 per second for 720p video. Here’s an overview of what’s new: Fast and cost-effective at scale Beyond the lower price, the workflow keeps costs down: you can draft fast at 360p or 720p, fix a detail with a follow-up edit instead of re-generating the entire clip, and then upscale your best creations to 1080p or 4K. Longer clips up to 15 seconds You can now generate and edit videos natively up to 15 seconds long, up from 10 seconds with Omni 1.1. You can also specify duration in one-second increments from 3 to 15 seconds, giving you room to tell complete stories, create product explainers, or produce full social ad spots in a single generation. Better reference adherence You can guide generation combining character, product, or style images, short motion clips (up to three seconds), and audio cues — and Omni 1.2 Flash holds onto those details from start to finish. Faces, garments, packaging typography, and brand colors stay consistent across camera angles, making it easy to turn existing product photography or character sheets into virtual try-on clips, catalog spins, and branded video ads. Combining one model photo with front-and-back product shots of three outfits, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generates a 15-second virtual try-on sequence across 360-degree turns and match cuts while keeping the model’s identity and each garment’s cut, drape, and back details consistent. More consistent results You can maintain stronger character, object, and scene consistency from the first to the last frame, with less visual drift or morphing across motion and camera transitions. Whether you’re interpolating between a first and last keyframe, or extending a clip to build a longer sequence, products, characters, props, and environments stay consistent from shot to shot. Given the same static studio lighting exhibition poster and five-layer animation prompt, Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash does not match the reference image as closely as 1.2 does. Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash builds the poster sequentially layer by layer on the dusty-pink cyclorama rising the hexagonal plinth, assembling the ribbed glass, warm filament, faceted crystal, and coiled-cord letterforms for HALO, GLOW, and LUMEN, and locking every material, shadow, and typographic detail consistently through the final frame. Easier editing in conversation You can refine the same clip turn by turn — such as swapping a product or background, changing the lighting or weather, or switching the aspect ratio — instead of starting over from scratch. Multi-turn conversational editing works across full 15-second clips, making it easy to produce ad variants for different audiences and placements without re-briefing or re-generating. Starting from one generated clip, multi-turn conversational prompts swap the background turn by turn — from a striped pavilion tent to an oak forest, a stable with a white horse, a market fair, and a stone castle — while keeping both characters’ performances, armor reflections, and camera framing intact. More natural speech You can generate scenes with more fluid, natural-sounding dialogue, clearer lip-sync, and distinct multi-speaker conditioning. This will show up whether you’re directing multi-character dialogue in Flow , creating video explainers in Gemini for business , or creating polished, pro videos with avatars, music and narration in Google Vids . Conditioned on one conservatory scene image alongside four character, mouth, and one-second voice references, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash routes each sampled voice to the right character with expressive lip-sync and natural comedic timing across a 15-second animated scene. More controllable, cinematic look You can direct complex, continuous camera movements like sweeping FPV flythroughs to dramatic zoom-outs and orbits with significantly fewer unwanted jump cuts, steadier scale, and a more polished, cinematic look. Guided by two architectural reference photos, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash directs one continuous FPV drone flight across the piazza, through the bronze doors, and up through the Pantheon’s coffered dome to the oculus with zero jump cuts. Longer clips with smoother motion and tighter consistency Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generates clips up to 15 seconds long that hold references together better than before. You can scroll through to see characters, text, and camera moves stay consistent across longer shots, multiple turns and transitions with no cuts. 15 second long clips: Turns one style frame into a 4-shot, 15-second macro science explainer with accurately spelled, motion-tracked callouts. Multi-turn motion transfer: Generates a rippling octopus in Turn 1, then replaces it in Turn 2 with a dancer whose gown mirrors the exact fluid motion. First-to-last frame consistency (1.1 vs. 1.2): Connects an exterior start frame and interior end frame in one continuous camera push in 1.2 Flash. You can see subtle differences like the cats on the roof, the soup ladle turning into chopsticks, and some other minor changes. Unbroken crash zoom-out: Pulls continuously from a tight shoreline close-up to an aerial island vista in one 10-second shot with natural scale and zero cuts. Real-world results, from creatives to global brands Businesses, startups, and creatives are already using Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash in their workflows. And for the first time, Gemini Omni is now generally available, backed by Google Cloud’s enterprise-grade infrastructure and security. Provisioned Throughput is available, and outputs carry an imperceptible SynthID watermark. Get started with Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash While development is ongoing to further improve things like fast sports action, rapid script changes and complex physics, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash is ideal for businesses, developers, and creators producing videos at scale. You can get started with Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash today as it rolls out across Google’s products and developer platforms: For developers using the Gemini API: Prototype in Google AI Studio , explore interactive starter apps, and check out the developer documentation and pricing . For businesses: Try it in the Google Cloud console , and build enterprise solutions with the API . For everyone using Google apps: Direct scenes and multi-turn edits in Flow , generate 15-second clips at no additional cost in Google Vids with a Google account or Google Workspace subscription, create 15-second videos in the Gemini app (rolling out to Google AI Ultra subscribers), and scale video campaigns in Google Ads . items.title: MCP Explained
items.articleText: Model Context Protocol What is MCP? An open standard for connecting AI apps to the tools and data they use. A server says what it can do, the app shows that to the model, and when the model wants something the app calls the server and hands the result back. Host the AI app you use: Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, an agent Server a small program exposing tools, data or prompts Model decides what to use; never talks to a server directly Not REST JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout or one HTTP endpoint, and servers can talk back Not just JSON-RPC JSON-RPC is the envelope. MCP defines what goes in it: the methods, capability negotiation, transports and auth Start the lessons → or jump to Tools · the spec time machine · Break it Model Context Protocol Lessons Spec Spec Network Sequence Message flow Step Reset # From To Method Info Not in the MCP spec A harness implementation detail, not part of MCP. Nothing new on the wire: the client and servers still speak plain tools/list and tools/call . Message MCP spec 2025-11-25. Token counts are illustrative. ## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). This release is signed with the key introduced in [commit `e82a3c6`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the published signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.108.1
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.108.1/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.108.1
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

items.summary: Humanoid developer Agility Robotics ended its first day of trading on the Nasdaq just 2% above where it started, at $11.49. The post How did Agility Robotics perform on its first day on the stock market? appeared first on The Robot Report .
items.articleText: Agility says its Digit 5 humanoids can lift up to 50 lb. | Source: Agility Robotics Earlier today, Agility Robotics began trading on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker “AGLT.” The company claimed that it is “the first pure-play legged humanoid company to go public.” Agility started the day trading at $11.26 per share, above the initial $10 per share price used in the SPAC deal. It was a day of ups and downs, as it was for many tech stocks. It hit its lowest price at $8.40, and its highest at $12.15. The company ended up closing the day trading slightly above (2%) where it had started, at $11.49. Other pure-play robotics providers did not fare so well. Serve Robotics , another publicly traded robotics company that offers sidewalk delivery robots, ended down 12.45%. Surgical robotics leader Intuitive Surgical ended down 2.82%. Symbotic , which provides end-to-end warehouse automation, ended down 2.47%. In addition, PROCEPT BioRobotics Corp. , which provides robotic aquablation therapy, ended down 6.42%. While Unitree , another humanoid robotics provider, doesn’t trade on the Nasdaq, it is public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange’s STR Market. It’s one of the only other publicly traded humanoid robot providers. Unitree first debuted on the market at 150.80 yuan ($22.55 U.S.), and saw some quick success, hitting a high of 1,100 yuan ($164.46) that day. Just a few weeks after debuting on the market, it was down almost 53% from its first-day high. The company is still working to climb back up to those numbers. In addition, China has reportedly tightened its own requirements for initial public offerings for humanoid robot startups. Technology and AI-related stocks struggle across markets Note that the entire Nasdaq is down 5.52% today, which means Agility was beating this overall trend. Much of these losses were concentrated in AI -related stocks. NVIDIA ended the day down 9.26% from its opening price. AMD ended down 17.26%, while Qualcomm dropped 9.49%. Microsoft was down 3.58%. Rockwell Automation was down 14.15%. Other markets have had some of their worst days since April 2025. The S&P 500 dropped 4.36%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 3.44%. This week’s midterm elections have caused the markets to fluctuate. While they saw some sharp gains yesterday, many of those gains dissipated today. Today’s losses have a lot to do with investor uncertainty around future data center buildouts with a now Democratically controlled Senate and House. What comes next for Agility Robotics From left to right, Cassie and Digit through the years. | Source: Agility Robotics The Robot Report will be watching Agility’s performance on the markets in the coming months. Already, the company alluded to adding more robots to its portfolio. The Robot Report also broke the news about Agility exploring wheel-based robots in September 2026. Peggy Johnson, Agility’s CEO, talked more about this plan in a recent video. In the video, she mentioned the possible addition of a smaller bipedal form factor to the company’s lineup. Agility claimed that for its newest Digit 5 , it has more than $300 million in committed multiyear orders, subject to contractual milestones and product specifications. It expects to begin Digit 5 deliveries to early-access customers in 2027. Agility’s public offering, which it conducted after completing a merger with special-purpose acquisition company (SPAC ) Churchill Capital Corp XI, will provide around $465 million in gross proceeds before expenses. items.title: How Ambi Robotics helps its customers prepare for peak season
items.summary: Ambi Robotics' co-founder and COO Stephen McKinley says the company is installing eight new systems at customer sites before peak season. The post How Ambi Robotics helps its customers prepare for peak season appeared first on The Robot Report .
items.articleText: The AmbiSort B Series can streamline final-mile deliver operations with automated induction, scanning, and ‘end-to-end’ sortation. | Source: Ambi Robotics As Black Friday and the start of peak season draw near, logistics providers across the country are getting ready for the rush. Each year, these providers could see a 25% to 40% increase in throughput, according to Stephen McKinley, co-founder and chief operating officer at Ambi Robotics. This year, Ambi is expecting its customers to experience a 9% to 10% increase compared with peak season last year. “Despite anything that might be going on in the economy, volume continues to ramp and e-commerce spending remains high,” McKinley told The Robot Report . “That puts familiar pressures on our clients to perform in all of their individual sites, and we’re feeling that pressure also, because our systems are core to their functions.” For Ambi, preparing for the season means installing new systems at eight facilities before peak season starts. “Most of those new sites are with this new version of AmbiSort , and though that’s not a new product, it’s definitely a new variation,” said McKinley. “We’re excited about supporting that through peak season, and we want to make sure that goes perfectly, of course, for our customers.” The Berkeley, Calif.-based company is also working to ensure that its team members will be readily available for logistics customers when they need them. “We move into a more reactive state of being, where we’ll have about half of the team traveling around to different sites to check in with what’s going on, and the other half of the team is ready to jump to solve issues as they come up,” McKinley said. How to increase throughput without adding new systems While some of Ambi Robotics’ customers plan to have more systems go live for peak season, there are other ways to increase throughput, McKinley said. “[Customers] will often add more shifts into existing operations or bring on more people to be working alongside our systems, so we can help with training,” he noted. “We offer more training to customers right before peak season to make sure they know how to effectively use the systems.” Properly training the operators working with robots on a daily basis can make a big difference in how the system performs. “Over the course of the year, we’re tracking how the systems are performing all the time,” said McKinley. “The performance of the systems is related to the inherent quality of that piece of machinery, which doesn’t really fluctuate, but also related to how the customer interacts with that machine and how attentive they are to it, or how well trained the operators are. So, we can help by stepping in and making sure that everybody knows what to do and has the right mindset when they’re approaching their system.” Ambi decreases downtime, rolls out incremental improvements Nobody wants a robot to fail, but they especially don’t want a robot to fail when they need to handle a massive increase in volume. This means reducing downtime is even more important for Ambi Robotics right now. To do this, the company forward-deploys spare parts to different sites. “Normally, we would have spare inventory here at our headquarters in Berkeley, and we would send things out as needed. That spares inventory is also what we use to pull form to build new systems,” McKinley said. “During peak seasons, we’ll bring in more spares and then deploy those out to specific locations in the East Coast that are hubs of customer activity.” For example, McKinley said Cincinnati is a central zone for a lot of the Ambi’s installs in the Midwest. “We’ll even go so far as to put spare computers or spare high critical items at each site that will carry more inventory at customer locations during peak season,” he continued. When it comes to rolling out improvements in its AI systems, Ambi takes a conservative approach. “We’ve been a physical AI company since 2018 when we started. We know how important it is to have systems out there in the world that are performing at predictable levels. So, we don’t have systems that are self-improving over time,” McKinley said. “As we generate more data from our systems, we’ll use that to retrain our systems and then process that improvement through an A/B test within a controlled environment to see what happens before we roll it out into the rest of the field.” When customers need help from Ambi, they will always speak with a person While it’s important to improve the technology, roll out new systems, and add more shifts, McKinley said it’s just as important for Ambi to build trust with its customers. “The people who will be answering the phones for our support hotline are the people who will go to the facilities and do the training and make the fixes,” he explained. “I think that’s very important, because we’re building a layer of trust with the operators and with the people on site who need to maintain the systems in our absence, and the management who’s on site.” “When they pick up the phone, they’ll know the voice on the other end, and that person will be familiar with them,” McKinley added. “That’s helped build trust significantly. That trust has been, in my opinion, the most important factor for those large customers to be adopting physical AI in the real world.” Instead of using AI to directly interact with customers, Ambi has developed an AI system to help its employees more quickly solve problems for its customers. This AI system also makes it easier for Ambi to onboard new employees, McKinley said. “We’ve been working on basically collecting all the data from our support tickets and then feeding that into our own AI model to assist in support. We have a very lean, very small team,” he said. “Now, we’ve got these AI assistants that are helping us keep track of performance on sites, then predict when things might be going wrong, and then helping us as a support organization.” Submit your innovation now! items.title: Chinese regulators block SoftBank’s $5.4B acquisition of ABB Robotics
items.summary: Chinese authorities blocked the deal over concerns about robot data being transferred overseas and used to train AI models. The post Chinese regulators block SoftBank’s $5.4B acquisition of ABB Robotics appeared first on The Robot Report .
items.articleText: ABB Robotics has about 7,000 employees, and its U.S. headquarters and factory are in Auburn Hills, Mich. | Source: ABB Robotics It has been more than a year since ABB announced it singed an agreement to sell its robotics division to the Japanese tech giant SoftBank Group. The $5.375 billion deal is now being blocked by Chinese regulators, ABB confirmed to The Robot Report . China ‘s Office of the Working Mechanism for Foreign Investment Security Review has prohibited the acquisition in the country. Authorities expressed concerns about robotics data being transferred overseas and used to train AI models, according to The Financial Times , which first reported that the deal was blocked. You may be wondering why Chinese regulators have so much say in a Japanese company acquiring a Zurich-based industrial automation provider , but China makes up a major portion of ABB’s revenue. For the entire FY 2025 , ABB Robotics saw $928,000 in orders from China, an increase from the $662,000 in orders it brought in from China in 2024. This is a growing region for ABB. In Q3 2026 , ABB Robotics saw a 32% increase in business in China alone. ABB also manufacturers a significant number of robots in its Shanghai factory. About 90% of its machines built for Chinese customers are manufactured locally, employing thousands of people in the country. Looking ahead, ABB said it and SoftBank are “in close dialogue and are working constructively on the transaction.” Is the robotics industry becoming a new political battleground? This news comes as global politics becomes increasingly important in the world of robotics. This isn’t the first time China has blocked an international deal citing national security concerns. In April, the country prevented Meta from acquiring Manus, an AI startup that was founded in China but then relocated to Singapore, for $2 billion. Here in the U.S., the federal government has taken steps to slow down foreign robot suppliers within the country. Just last week, U.S. President Donald J. Trump said the secretary of commerce had submitted a Section 232 report about the national security effects of imports of robotics and industrial machinery, as well as related parts and components. The Section 232 statement specifically cited “advanced robots — such as autonomous robots, humanoid and quadruped robots, and autonomous ground vehicles” as providing direct support to the U.S. military. While it’s unclear right now what this will mean for the robotics industry, it could lead to tariffs on foreign-made robots. Already, the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has banned new foreign-made advanced robotic devices, including mobile robots such as humanoids and quadrupeds. The FCC said these machines could create create supply chain vulnerabilities and pose a cybersecurity risk to American critical infrastructure. items.articleText: AI agents do more than generate answers. They search for information, query databases, write and test code and take action. Each of those steps relies on a CPU, with agents moving between GPU reasoning and CPU execution throughout a task. As businesses put more agents to work, AI factories need CPUs that can execute those steps quickly and support many agents at once, all within the limits of available power. What this means: AI infrastructure providers need to support more agents without making each one wait longer to get work done. And critically, AI factories are power limited. This means operators need to choose infrastructure that maximizes the work done for every watt. Why it matters: NVIDIA Vera delivers both fast agent performance and high capacity per watt within a single CPU. That gives providers one CPU for a range of agent workloads, rather than having to mix and match fast and dense x86 parts to balance speed and capacity. The data that proves it: In a 100-megawatt data center comparison, NVIDIA found that a single Vera CPU performs better than the fastest x86 CPU and the most energy-efficient x86 CPU. Vera delivers industry-leading agent speed while enabling 1.6x more agents per watt versus the fastest x86 CPU. Vera delivers 2x faster agent speed with leading energy efficiency compared with the most energy-efficient x86 CPU. Partners are already putting Vera to work. Early adopters see the same exceptional performance in production-style tests: Perplexity : Ran agentic coding tasks 1.5x faster with Vera than on traditional CPUs. Perplexity plans to deploy Vera in an upcoming production system. DeepInfra : Delivered up to 2.2x speed of the best x86 processor on agentic orchestration for its production agent workload, achieving the fastest of the four architectures tested. ClickHouse : Its standard binary, with no Vera-specific tuning, scaled near-linearly across 176 cores and topped the ClickBench hardware leaderboard. DuckLabs : Achieved about 1.5x the median TPC-H SF1000 performance of an Intel Xeon 6 baseline. Daytona : Brought 1,000 agent sandboxes online in 10.8 seconds, and achieved 12.7 completed jobs per second at 2,000 concurrent sandboxes, using Vera versus 88.4 seconds with x86. Modal : Achieved up to 2x sandbox throughput per core versus comparable x86 hardware, with gains that grow under heavy load. Learn more about the NVIDIA Vera CPU . report.cross_insight: - 해석: 로봇 현장 데이터의 국외 이전 및 AI 모델 학습 활용이 규제 당국의 안보 심사 대상으로 부상한 한편, 실제 산업 현장에서는 자율 개선 대신 통제된 A/B 테스트 기반의 보수적 배포 방식이 채택되고 있습니다 [15, 16].
report.section_robotics:
- **ManyForge**: ROS 비의존 코어(C++/Python)와 드래그 앤 드롭 비헤이비어 트리 GUI(Composer)를 제공하며 실시간 기능은 C++로 구현된 로봇 매니퓰레이션 프레임워크가 베타(Beta) 단계로 공개되었습니다 [1].
- **Robotiq ROS 패키지**: Humble, Jazzy, Lyrical, Rolling 배포판의 robotiq_controllers 및 robotiq_description 패키지 유지관리 저장소가 PickNikRobotics에서 공식 robotiq/robotiq-ros로 이전되며 버전이 0.0.1에서 1.x로 상향됩니다 [2].
report.section_devtools:
- **GPT-6 Cyber**: OpenAI에 따르면 허가된 범위 내에서 악용 가능한 취약점을 탐지하고 보안 패치를 개발하도록 훈련된 사이버 보안 특화 모델입니다 [6].
- **Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash**: DeepMind에 따르면 15초 영상 네이티브 생성과 멀티턴 대화형 편집을 지원하며 720p 기준 초당 0.07달러로 이전 버전 대비 비용을 30% 낮췄습니다 [8].
- **Claude Code**: v2.1.317 이상에서 웹 검색 시 User-Agent 헤더를 통해 사용자 이메일이 전송되던 동작을 확정적으로 차단하기 위해 기본 플러그인 cc-plugin-privacy가 도입되었습니다 [9].
- **Model Context Protocol**: AI 애플리케이션(호스트)과 외부 도구 및 데이터를 JSON-RPC 기반으로 표준화하여 연결하는 개방형 프로토콜입니다 [10].
- **Anthropic Python SDK v2.6.0**: ramp limit 오류 코드 및 외부 키(External Key) 검증 실패 에러 코드가 추가되고 플랫폼 클라이언트 예외 처리가 개선되었습니다 [11].
- **LiteLLM v1.108.1**: cosign 기반 Docker 컨테이너 이미지 무결성 검증을 지원하며 LTS(1.108.x) 브랜치의 수정 사항이 백포트되었습니다 [13].
- **NVIDIA Vera CPU**: NVIDIA 주장에 따르면 100MW 데이터센터 환경에서 단일 Vera CPU가 최고 성능의 x86 CPU 대비 전력당 1.6배 더 많은 AI 에이전트를 지원합니다 [17].
report.section_industry:
- **Agility Robotics**: Churchill Capital Corp XI와의 SPAC 합병 완료 후 종목 코드 AGLT로 나스닥에 상장하여 시작가 대비 2% 상승한 11.49달러에 첫날 거래를 마쳤습니다 [14].
- **Ambi Robotics**: 물류 성수기를 앞두고 고객사 8개 시설에 AmbiSort 새 변형 시스템을 신규 설치하며 수집 데이터 기반 A/B 테스트 검증 후 배포하는 보수적 방식을 적용하고 있습니다 [15].
- **중국 당국의 소프트뱅크 ABB 로보틱스 인수 불허**: 중국 외국인투자안보심사기구는 로봇 데이터의 해외 이전 및 AI 모델 학습 우려를 이유로 소프트뱅크의 53억 7,500만 달러 규모 ABB 로보틱스 인수를 불허했습니다 [16].

entries.title: ManyForge 매니퓰레이션 프레임워크 출시
entries.reason: ROS 비의존 코어 설계와 GUI 기반 비헤이비어 트리 작성 환경을 갖춘 매니퓰레이션 프레임워크 공개 정보를 제공합니다.

facts.statement: ManyForge의 핵심 컴포넌트는 C++ 또는 Python으로 작성되며 ROS에 의존하지 않고, 실시간 기능은 C++로 구현됩니다.
facts.quote: all core ManyForge components are C++ or Python and don’t depend on ROS.

entries.title: Robotiq ROS 패키지 유지관리 저장소 이전 안내
entries.reason: Robotiq 그리퍼 관련 ROS 2 공식 패키지의 저장소 이전 및 버전 업데이트에 따른 호환성 변경 정보를 전달합니다.

facts.statement: Humble, Jazzy, Lyrical, Rolling 배포판의 robotiq_controllers 및 robotiq_description 패키지가 기존 PickNikRobotics에서 robotiq-ros로 이전되어 릴리스됩니다.
facts.quote: The robotiq_controllers and robotiq_description packages on Humble, Jazzy, Lyrical and Rolling will soon be released from robotiq/robotiq-ros instead of PickNikRobotics/ros2_robotiq_gripper

entries.title: OpenAI GPT-6 Cyber 모델 발표
entries.reason: 허가된 범위 내에서 보안 취약점을 탐지하고 패치를 개발하도록 훈련된 보안 특화 AI 모델의 공개 소식을 다룹니다.

facts.statement: OpenAI가 취약점 탐지 및 수정안 개발을 위해 허가된 범위 내에서 작동하도록 훈련된 보안 모델 GPT-6 Cyber를 발표했습니다.
facts.quote: Introducing GPT‑6 Cyber, OpenAI’s cybersecurity model for finding exploitable vulnerabilities and developing fixes, trained to stay within authorized scope.

entries.title: Google DeepMind Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash 공개
entries.reason: 15초 네이티브 영상 생성 및 멀티턴 대화형 편집 기능을 추가하고 생성 비용을 절감한 영상 생성 모델 정보를 제공합니다.

facts.statement: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash는 15초 길이 영상 생성과 멀티턴 대화식 편집 기능 및 개선된 참조 일관성을 제공합니다.
facts.quote: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash introduces native 15-second video creation, multi-turn conversational editing capabilities, and enhanced reference following.

entries.title: Claude Code의 사용자 이메일 전송 이슈 및 보호 플러그인 도입
entries.reason: Claude Code가 웹 검색 시 User-Agent 헤더에 사용자 이메일을 포함하던 동작과 이를 차단하는 기본 플러그인 적용 현황을 공유합니다.

facts.statement: Anthropic 관계자는 v2.1.317 이상에서 User-Agent를 통한 이메일 유출 동작을 차단하기 위한 기본 모듈인 cc-plugin-privacy를 도입했다고 밝혔습니다.
facts.quote: We introduced a built-in mod called cc-plugin-privacy to deterministically block this behavior in v2.1.317 and later

entries.title: Model Context Protocol(MCP) 개요 및 표준 설명
entries.reason: AI 애플리케이션과 외부 도구 및 데이터를 표준 방식으로 연결하는 MCP의 기본 구조와 통신 방식을 파악할 수 있습니다.

facts.statement: MCP는 AI 애플리케이션을 도구 및 데이터와 연결하기 위해 JSON-RPC 기반으로 설계된 공개 표준입니다.
facts.quote: An open standard for connecting AI apps to the tools and data they use.

entries.title: Anthropic SDK Python v2.6.0 릴리스
entries.reason: Ramp limit 에러 코드 추가 및 클라우드 플랫폼 클라이언트 예외 처리 개선 등 최신 파이썬 SDK 변경 사항을 안내합니다.

facts.statement: Anthropic Python SDK v2.6.0에 ramp limit 에러 코드 및 외부 키 검증 실패에 대한 에러 코드가 추가되었습니다.
facts.quote: api: add error code for ramp limit errors

entries.title: LiteLLM v1.108.1 릴리스 및 Docker 이미지 서명 검증 지원
entries.reason: cosign을 활용한 컨테이너 이미지 무결성 검증 절차와 LTS 브랜치 패치 내역을 전달합니다.

facts.statement: LiteLLM의 모든 Docker 이미지는 cosign으로 서명되며 지정된 공개 키 또는 릴리스 태그를 통해 검증할 수 있습니다.
facts.quote: All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign .

entries.title: Agility Robotics의 나스닥 상장 첫날 거래 결과
entries.reason: 휴머노이드 로봇 기업 Agility Robotics의 SPAC 합병 후 나스닥 상장 첫날 주가 변동 및 조달 자금 현황을 다룹니다.

facts.statement: Agility Robotics가 종목 코드 AGLT로 나스닥 시장에서 거래를 시작하며 상장 첫날 시작가 대비 2% 상승 마감했습니다.
facts.quote: Earlier today, Agility Robotics began trading on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker “AGLT.”

entries.title: Ambi Robotics의 물류 성수기 대비 시스템 구축 전략
entries.reason: 전자상거래 성수기를 앞두고 8개 현장에 AmbiSort 시스템을 증설하고 물리 AI 모델의 안정적 배포 방식을 적용한 사례를 소개합니다.

facts.statement: Ambi Robotics는 물류 성수기 시작 전에 고객사 8개 시설에 AmbiSort 새 변형 시스템을 신규 설치하고 있습니다.
facts.quote: For Ambi, preparing for the season means installing new systems at eight facilities before peak season starts.

entries.title: 중국 당국의 소프트뱅크 ABB 로보틱스 인수 불허 결정
entries.reason: 해외 로봇 데이터 이전 및 AI 학습 활용 우려로 인해 53억 7,500만 달러 규모의 로봇 사업부 인수가 차단된 산업 규제 소식을 전합니다.

facts.statement: 중국 외국인투자안보심사기구는 데이터 해외 이전 및 AI 모델 학습 우려를 이유로 소프트뱅크의 ABB 로보틱스 인수를 불허했습니다.

entries.title: NVIDIA의 AI 에이전트 워크로드용 Vera CPU 공개
entries.reason: AI 에이전트의 데이터 조회 및 코드 실행 워크로드를 지원하기 위한 단일 CPU 아키텍처 성능 지표를 전달합니다.

facts.statement: NVIDIA는 100메가와트 데이터센터 환경 비교 테스트에서 Vera CPU가 가장 빠른 x86 CPU 대비 전력당 1.6배 더 많은 에이전트를 지원한다고 밝혔습니다.

The best part for UX is the GUI (the Composer): you build programs as behavior trees in a dedicated drag&drop editor allowing most of the functionalities you’d expect to ease programming a manipulator: a 3D scene where you place and move objects with gizmos, or edit them in the object editor; manual moves with a ghost robot that shows where the arm will end up (collision-checked) before you send it; Draft + Apply, so nothing changes on the cell until you say so; live robot state, I/O and stop handling right in the same window. Honestly, it’s a huge application and it’s still in Beta, and I’m the first to recognize it would require more documentation and educational material to be understood correctly. I’m working on it. In the meantime, I’m making it as much operable and discoverable by LLMs as possible, so any frontier model should be able to install it and explain how it works in detail without much trouble. A note about the development process: the public repository is for deployment and I’m using AI coding assistants heavily. But all development is based on a (for now private) Specs repo that is the authority on what each and every component of ManyForge is, what it does and how, in painstaking detail. Every change is checked against the Specs, reviewed independently and run through thousands of tests, sanitizer builds and stress runs, plus live checks on Mock, Isaac Sim and the real robot, so even structural changes don’t break execution. Still, since I am the one doing all the architectural and design decisions, I’m pretty sure this could be better and I’m very open to discussing architectural and design choices, hardening, and also to introduce useful functionalities. 2 Likes Related topics Topic Replies Views Activity ManyMove - A simple manipulation framework - What, Why and How Projects 2 517 June 11, 2025 ManyMove – C++/Python Behavior Trees for Robot Manipulators (Looking for Feedback and Tips) Projects 9 1122 March 28, 2025 [Release] LinkForge v1.4.0: A Programmable Robot Description Engine (URDF/SRDF) ROS General release , ros2 , simulation , robotics , physics 2 190 June 2, 2026 ManyMove integration with Isaac SIM 5.0 ROS General 0 241 August 30, 2025 LinkForge v1.3.0 — The Linter & Bridge for Robotics ROS General release , ros2 , simulation , ros2_control , open-source 0 188 March 2, 2026

Better reference adherence You can guide generation combining character, product, or style images, short motion clips (up to three seconds), and audio cues — and Omni 1.2 Flash holds onto those details from start to finish. Faces, garments, packaging typography, and brand colors stay consistent across camera angles, making it easy to turn existing product photography or character sheets into virtual try-on clips, catalog spins, and branded video ads. Combining one model photo with front-and-back product shots of three outfits, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generates a 15-second virtual try-on sequence across 360-degree turns and match cuts while keeping the model’s identity and each garment’s cut, drape, and back details consistent. Whether you’re interpolating between a first and last keyframe, or extending a clip to build a longer sequence, products, characters, props, and environments stay consistent from shot to shot. Given the same static studio lighting exhibition poster and five-layer animation prompt, Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash does not match the reference image as closely as 1.2 does. Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash builds the poster sequentially layer by layer on the dusty-pink cyclorama rising the hexagonal plinth, assembling the ribbed glass, warm filament, faceted crystal, and coiled-cord letterforms for HALO, GLOW, and LUMEN, and locking every material, shadow, and typographic detail consistently through the final frame. Starting from one generated clip, multi-turn conversational prompts swap the background turn by turn — from a striped pavilion tent to an oak forest, a stable with a white horse, a market fair, and a stone castle — while keeping both characters’ performances, armor reflections, and camera framing intact. More natural speech You can generate scenes with more fluid, natural-sounding dialogue, clearer lip-sync, and distinct multi-speaker conditioning. selectedItems.articleText: Model Context Protocol What is MCP? An open standard for connecting AI apps to the tools and data they use. A server says what it can do, the app shows that to the model, and when the model wants something the app calls the server and hands the result back. Host the AI app you use: Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, an agent Server a small program exposing tools, data or prompts Model decides what to use; never talks to a server directly Not REST JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout or one HTTP endpoint, and servers can talk back Not just JSON-RPC JSON-RPC is the envelope. MCP defines what goes in it: the methods, capability negotiation, transports and auth Start the lessons → or jump to Tools · the spec time machine · Break it Model Context Protocol Lessons Spec Spec Network Sequence Message flow Step Reset # From To Method Info Not in the MCP spec A harness implementation detail, not part of MCP. ## Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/overview/). This release is signed with the key introduced in [commit `e82a3c6`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065).

**Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):**

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the published signing key:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/e82a3c646908ba0a6ee0beddc4310d7a6cac4065/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.108.1
```

**Verify using the release tag (convenience):**

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

```bash
cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.108.1/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.108.1
```

Expected output:

```
The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key
```

selectedItems.summary: Humanoid developer Agility Robotics ended its first day of trading on the Nasdaq just 2% above where it started, at $11.49. The post How did Agility Robotics perform on its first day on the stock market? appeared first on The Robot Report .
selectedItems.articleText: Agility says its Digit 5 humanoids can lift up to 50 lb. | Source: Agility Robotics Earlier today, Agility Robotics began trading on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker “AGLT.” The company claimed that it is “the first pure-play legged humanoid company to go public.” Agility started the day trading at $11.26 per share, above the initial $10 per share price used in the SPAC deal. It was a day of ups and downs, as it was for many tech stocks. It hit its lowest price at $8.40, and its highest at $12.15. The company ended up closing the day trading slightly above (2%) where it had started, at $11.49. Other pure-play robotics providers did not fare so well. Serve Robotics , another publicly traded robotics company that offers sidewalk delivery robots, ended down 12.45%. Surgical robotics leader Intuitive Surgical ended down 2.82%. Symbotic , which provides end-to-end warehouse automation, ended down 2.47%. In addition, PROCEPT BioRobotics Corp. , which provides robotic aquablation therapy, ended down 6.42%. While Unitree , another humanoid robotics provider, doesn’t trade on the Nasdaq, it is public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange’s STR Market. It’s one of the only other publicly traded humanoid robot providers. Unitree first debuted on the market at 150.80 yuan ($22.55 U.S.), and saw some quick success, hitting a high of 1,100 yuan ($164.46) that day. Just a few weeks after debuting on the market, it was down almost 53% from its first-day high. The company is still working to climb back up to those numbers. In addition, China has reportedly tightened its own requirements for initial public offerings for humanoid robot startups. Technology and AI-related stocks struggle across markets Note that the entire Nasdaq is down 5.52% today, which means Agility was beating this overall trend. Much of these losses were concentrated in AI -related stocks. NVIDIA ended the day down 9.26% from its opening price. AMD ended down 17.26%, while Qualcomm dropped 9.49%. Microsoft was down 3.58%. Rockwell Automation was down 14.15%. Other markets have had some of their worst days since April 2025. The S&P 500 dropped 4.36%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 3.44%. This week’s midterm elections have caused the markets to fluctuate. While they saw some sharp gains yesterday, many of those gains dissipated today. Today’s losses have a lot to do with investor uncertainty around future data center buildouts with a now Democratically controlled Senate and House. What comes next for Agility Robotics From left to right, Cassie and Digit through the years. | Source: Agility Robotics The Robot Report will be watching Agility’s performance on the markets in the coming months. Already, the company alluded to adding more robots to its portfolio. The Robot Report also broke the news about Agility exploring wheel-based robots in September 2026. Peggy Johnson, Agility’s CEO, talked more about this plan in a recent video. In the video, she mentioned the possible addition of a smaller bipedal form factor to the company’s lineup. Agility claimed that for its newest Digit 5 , it has more than $300 million in committed multiyear orders, subject to contractual milestones and product specifications. It expects to begin Digit 5 deliveries to early-access customers in 2027. Agility’s public offering, which it conducted after completing a merger with special-purpose acquisition company (SPAC ) Churchill Capital Corp XI, will provide around $465 million in gross proceeds before expenses. selectedItems.title: How Ambi Robotics helps its customers prepare for peak season
selectedItems.summary: Ambi Robotics' co-founder and COO Stephen McKinley says the company is installing eight new systems at customer sites before peak season. The post How Ambi Robotics helps its customers prepare for peak season appeared first on The Robot Report .
selectedItems.articleText: The AmbiSort B Series can streamline final-mile deliver operations with automated induction, scanning, and ‘end-to-end’ sortation. | Source: Ambi Robotics As Black Friday and the start of peak season draw near, logistics providers across the country are getting ready for the rush. Each year, these providers could see a 25% to 40% increase in throughput, according to Stephen McKinley, co-founder and chief operating officer at Ambi Robotics. This year, Ambi is expecting its customers to experience a 9% to 10% increase compared with peak season last year. “Despite anything that might be going on in the economy, volume continues to ramp and e-commerce spending remains high,” McKinley told The Robot Report . “That puts familiar pressures on our clients to perform in all of their individual sites, and we’re feeling that pressure also, because our systems are core to their functions.” For Ambi, preparing for the season means installing new systems at eight facilities before peak season starts. “Most of those new sites are with this new version of AmbiSort , and though that’s not a new product, it’s definitely a new variation,” said McKinley. “We’re excited about supporting that through peak season, and we want to make sure that goes perfectly, of course, for our customers.” The Berkeley, Calif.-based company is also working to ensure that its team members will be readily available for logistics customers when they need them. “We move into a more reactive state of being, where we’ll have about half of the team traveling around to different sites to check in with what’s going on, and the other half of the team is ready to jump to solve issues as they come up,” McKinley said. How to increase throughput without adding new systems While some of Ambi Robotics’ customers plan to have more systems go live for peak season, there are other ways to increase throughput, McKinley said. “[Customers] will often add more shifts into existing operations or bring on more people to be working alongside our systems, so we can help with training,” he noted. “We offer more training to customers right before peak season to make sure they know how to effectively use the systems.” Properly training the operators working with robots on a daily basis can make a big difference in how the system performs. “Over the course of the year, we’re tracking how the systems are performing all the time,” said McKinley. “The performance of the systems is related to the inherent quality of that piece of machinery, which doesn’t really fluctuate, but also related to how the customer interacts with that machine and how attentive they are to it, or how well trained the operators are. So, we can help by stepping in and making sure that everybody knows what to do and has the right mindset when they’re approaching their system.” Ambi decreases downtime, rolls out incremental improvements Nobody wants a robot to fail, but they especially don’t want a robot to fail when they need to handle a massive increase in volume. This means reducing downtime is even more important for Ambi Robotics right now. To do this, the company forward-deploys spare parts to different sites. “Normally, we would have spare inventory here at our headquarters in Berkeley, and we would send things out as needed. That spares inventory is also what we use to pull form to build new systems,” McKinley said. “During peak seasons, we’ll bring in more spares and then deploy those out to specific locations in the East Coast that are hubs of customer activity.” For example, McKinley said Cincinnati is a central zone for a lot of the Ambi’s installs in the Midwest. “We’ll even go so far as to put spare computers or spare high critical items at each site that will carry more inventory at customer locations during peak season,” he continued. When it comes to rolling out improvements in its AI systems, Ambi takes a conservative approach. “We’ve been a physical AI company since 2018 when we started. We know how important it is to have systems out there in the world that are performing at predictable levels. So, we don’t have systems that are self-improving over time,” McKinley said. “As we generate more data from our systems, we’ll use that to retrain our systems and then process that improvement through an A/B test within a controlled environment to see what happens before we roll it out into the rest of the field.” When customers need help from Ambi, they will always speak with a person While it’s important to improve the technology, roll out new systems, and add more shifts, McKinley said it’s just as important for Ambi to build trust with its customers. “The people who will be answering the phones for our support hotline are the people who will go to the facilities and do the training and make the fixes,” he explained. “I think that’s very important, because we’re building a layer of trust with the operators and with the people on site who need to maintain the systems in our absence, and the management who’s on site.” “When they pick up the phone, they’ll know the voice on the other end, and that person will be familiar with them,” McKinley added. “That’s helped build trust significantly. That trust has been, in my opinion, the most important factor for those large customers to be adopting physical AI in the real world.” Instead of using AI to directly interact with customers, Ambi has developed an AI system to help its employees more quickly solve problems for its customers. This AI system also makes it easier for Ambi to onboard new employees, McKinley said. “We’ve been working on basically collecting all the data from our support tickets and then feeding that into our own AI model to assist in support. We have a very lean, very small team,” he said. “Now, we’ve got these AI assistants that are helping us keep track of performance on sites, then predict when things might be going wrong, and then helping us as a support organization.” Submit your innovation now! selectedItems.title: Chinese regulators block SoftBank’s $5.4B acquisition of ABB Robotics
selectedItems.summary: Chinese authorities blocked the deal over concerns about robot data being transferred overseas and used to train AI models. The post Chinese regulators block SoftBank’s $5.4B acquisition of ABB Robotics appeared first on The Robot Report .
selectedItems.articleText: ABB Robotics has about 7,000 employees, and its U.S. headquarters and factory are in Auburn Hills, Mich. | Source: ABB Robotics It has been more than a year since ABB announced it singed an agreement to sell its robotics division to the Japanese tech giant SoftBank Group. The $5.375 billion deal is now being blocked by Chinese regulators, ABB confirmed to The Robot Report . China ‘s Office of the Working Mechanism for Foreign Investment Security Review has prohibited the acquisition in the country. Authorities expressed concerns about robotics data being transferred overseas and used to train AI models, according to The Financial Times , which first reported that the deal was blocked. You may be wondering why Chinese regulators have so much say in a Japanese company acquiring a Zurich-based industrial automation provider , but China makes up a major portion of ABB’s revenue. For the entire FY 2025 , ABB Robotics saw $928,000 in orders from China, an increase from the $662,000 in orders it brought in from China in 2024. This is a growing region for ABB. In Q3 2026 , ABB Robotics saw a 32% increase in business in China alone. ABB also manufacturers a significant number of robots in its Shanghai factory. About 90% of its machines built for Chinese customers are manufactured locally, employing thousands of people in the country. Looking ahead, ABB said it and SoftBank are “in close dialogue and are working constructively on the transaction.” Is the robotics industry becoming a new political battleground? This news comes as global politics becomes increasingly important in the world of robotics. This isn’t the first time China has blocked an international deal citing national security concerns. In April, the country prevented Meta from acquiring Manus, an AI startup that was founded in China but then relocated to Singapore, for $2 billion. Here in the U.S., the federal government has taken steps to slow down foreign robot suppliers within the country. Just last week, U.S. President Donald J. Trump said the secretary of commerce had submitted a Section 232 report about the national security effects of imports of robotics and industrial machinery, as well as related parts and components. The Section 232 statement specifically cited “advanced robots — such as autonomous robots, humanoid and quadruped robots, and autonomous ground vehicles” as providing direct support to the U.S. military. While it’s unclear right now what this will mean for the robotics industry, it could lead to tariffs on foreign-made robots. Already, the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has banned new foreign-made advanced robotic devices, including mobile robots such as humanoids and quadrupeds. The FCC said these machines could create create supply chain vulnerabilities and pose a cybersecurity risk to American critical infrastructure. selectedItems.articleText: AI agents do more than generate answers. They search for information, query databases, write and test code and take action. Each of those steps relies on a CPU, with agents moving between GPU reasoning and CPU execution throughout a task. As businesses put more agents to work, AI factories need CPUs that can execute those steps quickly and support many agents at once, all within the limits of available power. What this means: AI infrastructure providers need to support more agents without making each one wait longer to get work done. And critically, AI factories are power limited. This means operators need to choose infrastructure that maximizes the work done for every watt. Why it matters: NVIDIA Vera delivers both fast agent performance and high capacity per watt within a single CPU. That gives providers one CPU for a range of agent workloads, rather than having to mix and match fast and dense x86 parts to balance speed and capacity. The data that proves it: In a 100-megawatt data center comparison, NVIDIA found that a single Vera CPU performs better than the fastest x86 CPU and the most energy-efficient x86 CPU. Vera delivers industry-leading agent speed while enabling 1.6x more agents per watt versus the fastest x86 CPU. Vera delivers 2x faster agent speed with leading energy efficiency compared with the most energy-efficient x86 CPU. Partners are already putting Vera to work. Early adopters see the same exceptional performance in production-style tests: Perplexity : Ran agentic coding tasks 1.5x faster with Vera than on traditional CPUs. Perplexity plans to deploy Vera in an upcoming production system. DeepInfra : Delivered up to 2.2x speed of the best x86 processor on agentic orchestration for its production agent workload, achieving the fastest of the four architectures tested. ClickHouse : Its standard binary, with no Vera-specific tuning, scaled near-linearly across 176 cores and topped the ClickBench hardware leaderboard. DuckLabs : Achieved about 1.5x the median TPC-H SF1000 performance of an Intel Xeon 6 baseline. Daytona : Brought 1,000 agent sandboxes online in 10.8 seconds, and achieved 12.7 completed jobs per second at 2,000 concurrent sandboxes, using Vera versus 88.4 seconds with x86. Modal : Achieved up to 2x sandbox throughput per core versus comparable x86 hardware, with gains that grow under heavy load. Learn more about the NVIDIA Vera CPU .
